speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The runaway wheel also narrowly missed another motorcyclist as it tumbled across the road.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It was sheer luck that others did not come into contact with this wheel and suffer the consequences.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: That motorcyclist was the late Mr Slemat Rakisan.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We were fellow community leaders serving together in Jurong Group Representation Constituency (GRC).

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The hon Minister and Grassroots Advisor of Yuhua grassroots organisations (GROs), Ms Grace Fu, in her eulogy posting, described him as a "humble and compassionate leader" who also brought much laughter with his Tom Jones and Elvis Presley impersonations.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I met him just the weekend before he died at a community music event.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The randomness of the accident leading to his death remains disconcerting.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Just three months after the KJE accident, there was yet another instance of a loose wheel coming off a Malaysian-registered truck, this time, on the West Coast Highway.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This rolled across the lanes and smashed into a car travelling in the opposite direction.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Thankfully, the driver of the car only suffered a minor injury to his right ear.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Wheels come off the vehicles as a result of mechanical failures.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These unfortunate accidents illustrate how mechanical failure in heavy vehicles often lead to accidents that may cause serious injuries or fatalities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Regrettably, these two are not the only instances of accidents involving mechanical failure in heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In July last year, a private bus driver realised the brakes of the bus had failed and, to avoid a collision with the stationary cars in his path, he mounted a kerb intending to manoeuvre his vehicle into a nearby tree for a controlled crash.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Unfortunately, he hit a woman cycling home from work along a footway.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It was determined by the Coroner after an inquiry that the brake failure was due to a missing drain valve component, which led to the bus having no braking ability whatsoever.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In such fatal accidents caused by mechanical failure, as opposed to driver negligence or recklessness, these are often ruled as misadventures and there is little that the authorities can presently do to impose criminal liability for the accidents, although civil remedies, such as insurance claims, remain available.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This state of affairs is, with respect, unsatisfactory because the parties responsible for maintaining the critical component parts of the heavy vehicles that failed, escape criminal liability for causing the accidents.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I respectfully suggest that the Government consider imposing liability on the owners and operators of the heavy vehicles to hold them to account for accidents arising from mechanical failure that may be obviated through proper maintenance.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is well-known that a significant number of fatal accidents involve heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the workplace context, the figures of fatal accidents involving heavy vehicles are also concerning.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He also highlighted that in the first half of 2017, there were 379 injuries and seven fatalities caused by vehicle-related incidents.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This led to the implementation of new workplace vehicle safety initiatives, which is very welcomed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It appears that there are no publicly available studies which has been done to ascertain how many of these accidents involved mechanical failure.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What is clear is that such accidents do happen, whether in Singapore or overseas.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Common types of mechanical failures include malfunctioning brakes, faulty steering systems, faulty headlights or taillights, and tyre and wheel issues, such as worn tyres and overtightened wheel bolts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Under our current system, there are three separate regimes that deal with different aspects of road safety involving heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On one end, the Traffic Police's focus is on the culpability of the driver, such as for reckless or negligent driving, under the Road Traffic Act or, sometimes, the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This would cover accidents caused by the behaviour of drivers of heavy vehicles, such as speeding and red-running.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, whilst it is an offence under the Road Traffic Act for a person who causes a heavy motor vehicle to collide with any buildings or structures, there is no specific offence under the Act which attributes responsibility of the owners and operators of heavy vehicles for road traffic accidents caused by mechanical failure that is preventable.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Last year, a public bus driver was acquitted of the offence of rash driving.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He was accused of driving above the speed limit whilst negotiating a bend along the slip road of Bukit Timah Expressway into Dairy Farm Road.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: A passenger was killed and another was injured.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The driver testified that he experienced brake problems and, in his words, "engine runaway" which caused the bus to accelerate on its own.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The prosecution's expert witness testified that he found an air leak in one of the bus' air pipes which could have affected the brake efficiency, but he could not conduct a brake efficiency test due to the damage the bus sustained in the crash.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The learned District Judge accepted the driver's defence and acquitted him.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What is evident from the case is that there was no focus on the bus company to ascertain whether it had properly maintained the brake system of the bus.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is understandable because of the current legislation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) enforces the periodic vehicle inspection regime as well as the requirements under the Road Traffic (Motor Vehicles, Construction and Use) Rules which lay down the specifications for critical component parts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The objective is to minimise vehicular breakdown and road accidents.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the intervening period between inspections, there always remains the probability that vehicles are driven without proper maintenance as recommended by the vehicle manufacturers until just before the inspection.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is a moral hazard that must be addressed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: LTA does not routinely open an investigation to identify the responsible party behind the mechanical failure leading to the fatal accident.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For example, the Workplace Health and Safety Regulations stipulate that it is the duty of the owner of any vehicle used in a worksite to ensure that the vehicle is of good construction and is roadworthy.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It was recently reported in June 2018 that one out of every three deaths in the workplace last year was caused by a vehicular incident, making it the No 1 cause of workplace deaths last year.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: To address this issue, MOM has launched the new Drive Safe Work Safe campaign to raise awareness about good vehicular safety practices and is also trialling the use of devices that track and monitor the speed of heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Whilst the Workplace Health and Safety Act allows MOM to prosecute errant employers for safety lapses leading to injuries to workers, the Act is focused on addressing the safety, health and welfare of persons at work in workplaces.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It does not go so far as to cover situations where such vehicle-related safety lapses cause injury or death to members of the public.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: To illustrate, the late Mr Slemat’s accident case does not constitute a workplace incident as he was not a worker.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, if the driver of the trailer truck was injured, then it would be a workplace incident.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the joint MOM and Police circular I mentioned earlier, as well as in the Workplace Safety and Health Guidelines, it was recommended that, firstly, heavy vehicle owners should implement a regime for the maintenance of all vehicles in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations on the basis that a well-maintained vehicle is more likely to work better and last longer.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These records will serve as a "treasure trove" for investigators of fatal accidents looking into whether or not the owners and operators have contributed to the accident by not properly maintaining their heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The imposition of criminal liability on owners and operators of heavy vehicles for mechanical failures of critical component parts leading to fatal accidents would serve as a deterrence against skimping on the proper checks that should be conducted on heavy vehicles and reduce the incidents of such fatal accidents.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In this regard, I wish to highlight three practical points for consideration by the Government.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is important for the regulations to cover not just owners but operators.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is because it is not unusual for individuals to own heavy vehicles, such as cement mixers and tipper trucks.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These individuals then support operators, which tend to be the big companies, in activities, such as construction and logistics.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Practically, it is these operators who will have the greatest influence over the maintenance standards of vehicles used in their operations.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: From a liability viewpoint, it should suffice if the mechanical failure, as a result of lack of maintenance, played a contributory factor, as opposed to the effective factor, that led to the fatal accident.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Otherwise, we may create a loophole for errant owners and operators of heavy vehicles to take advantage of.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Properly maintained heavy vehicles are more likely to work better and last longer.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Hence, the interests of owners and operators of heavy vehicles should be aligned with this initiative.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Heavy vehicle owners and operators play an important role in ensuring that no other road user will be imperiled as a result of mechanical failure in critical component parts due to lack of maintenance.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The legislation must be updated to reflect this plain fact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Indeed, safety is an important part of these operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And my thoughts and condolences to Encik Slemat and his family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It was a tragic story that was shared with us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, LTA requires all in-use vehicles to be regularly inspected at LTA-authorised Inspection Centres (AICs), ensuring that they are roadworthy and that emission standards are met.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These inspections are conducted every six months to a year, depending on the type and age of the vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As the vehicles age and as they are used more intensively, frequency of inspection goes up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These inspections cover key vehicle components and systems, such as brakes, steering, tyres and exhaust systems, to ensure that they are in good working order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Besides these regular inspections, LTA and the Traffic Police also have powers to call up vehicles for ad hoc inspections to ensure their safety and roadworthiness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Heavy vehicles tend to be used more intensively and are, therefore, more prone to wear and tear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have imposed statutory lifespans on heavy vehicles to ensure that the population of heavy vehicles on our roads stays young.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is the vehicle owners' responsibility to ensure that their vehicles are properly maintained and pass LTA's vehicle inspection requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the case of heavy vehicles that are typically used for commercial purposes, the responsibility lies with the companies that own these heavy vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The companies are incentivised to ensure that their heavy vehicles are well-maintained, because those which fail the inspection will not be allowed to be used until the fault is rectified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will have an impact on their business operations and the companies will also have to bear the costs of additional inspections.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With regard to Mr Murali Pillai's suggestion to mandate a preventive maintenance regime, our view is that it is not necessary to be prescriptive about the maintenance regime as our inspection regime is already very frequent and stringent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: LTA takes an outcome-based approach, which balances the imperative to create a safe working and commuting environment with the regulatory burden on vehicle owners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such an outcome-based approach also leaves room for new technologies to be brought in very quickly to improve maintenance regimes and improve safety, rather than being very prescriptive of the technology and the process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Member has asked about the Government's powers to prosecute businesses which do not properly maintain their heavy vehicles and, as a result, cause fatal accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under the Workplace Safety and Health Act (WSHA), employers have a duty to take adequate measures to ensure the safety and health of their employees at work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes the proper maintenance of equipment used by their workers, including heavy vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Employers who fail in their duties under WSHA, regardless of whether it is an individual or body corporate, may be prosecuted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the case of a body corporate, the employer may face a fine of up to $500,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Persons, including body corporates, who cause death by a negligent act can also be charged under the Penal Code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Persons who have been found guilty may face imprisonment for a term up to two years, or a fine, or both.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This could include persons who were negligent in maintaining their vehicles, thereby directly leading to a fatal accident.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOM's Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) also provides for the payment of compensation to employees for injury or death suffered in the course of their employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Depending on the circumstances of the case, the compensation payable could be up to $262,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, accident victims can also seek legal recourse by taking those responsible for causing the accident to task through civil lawsuits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In summary, Mr Deputy Speaker, we do have a comprehensive framework of vehicular inspections and laws to hold vehicle owners responsible for ensuring their vehicles are roadworthy and safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Less than 5% of these accidents involved claims of mechanical failures, of which, some are still pending investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More often, heavy vehicle accidents are primarily caused by driving behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Even as we take errant drivers to task, it is even more important that we continue to work with companies to promote a safe driving culture and ensure that drivers have sufficient rest.
